The input grid contains a small number of blue (B) dots placed on a black (.) background. These blue dots form a diagonal line with a constant step size: each consecutive blue dot is offset from the previous one by the same number of rows down and the same number of columns to the right.

1. Identify all blue (B) cells and sort them by row (or equivalently by column, since they lie on a diagonal). 2. Compute the constant step between consecutive blue dots: Δrow = row difference, Δcol = column difference. 3. Starting from the last blue dot, repeatedly add (Δrow, Δcol) to generate new positions. 4. For each new position that falls within the grid boundaries, place a red (R) dot. Continue until the next position would fall outside the grid. 5. Leave all existing blue dots and the black background unchanged.

The grid is 15 rows by 15 columns with a black (.) background. Blue dots appear at regular diagonal intervals. The grid uses a 0-indexed coordinate system with (0,0) at the top-left corner.
